lead.headline: HSBC puts a Hong Kong dollar stablecoin in 2 million retail wallets while ASEAN central banks expand cross-border stablecoin rails
lead.tldr: Stablecoins are simultaneously breaking into retail banking and inter-governmental payment infrastructure, but regulatory pressure on issuers is intensifying just as adoption accelerates.

intro: Dear Founders, Investors, and Friends, today the stablecoin story splits in two: institutional rails going live in Asia and political scrutiny sharpening in Washington.

top_signals.title: Malaysia, Thailand join Singapore’s cross-border stablecoin push
top_signals.summary: Malaysia and Thailand have joined Singapore's BLOOM initiative to enhance cross-border payment systems. The collaboration focuses on utilizing stablecoins and tokenized deposits to streamline international transactions.
top_signals.why_it_matters: The BLOOM expansion signals that ASEAN monetary authorities are underwriting stablecoin infrastructure as a sovereign payment layer, which reprices the competitive moat for private issuers from technology to regulatory alignment.

top_signals.title: HSBC rolls out its first HKD stablecoin RedCoin to retail users
top_signals.summary: HSBC is launching its first HKD-pegged stablecoin, RedCoin, for retail users via the PayMe app. The integration allows users to perform peer-to-peer and peer-to-merchant payments using a dedicated in-app stablecoin wallet.
top_signals.why_it_matters: HSBC's retail stablecoin launch via PayMe means a systemically important bank is now collecting KYC'd user data on stablecoin behavior at scale, creating a template for how tradfi incumbents can capture the payment use case without ceding balance sheet to crypto-native issuers.

top_signals.title: New York seeks over $1.3 billion from NovaTech founders after couple fled the US
top_signals.summary: New York state is seeking over $1.3 billion from the founders of NovaTech after they fled the United States. The state alleges the company received $1.16 billion in crypto deposits, with a significant portion diverted to the founders' wallets.
top_signals.why_it_matters: The $1.3 billion NovaTech enforcement action demonstrates that state regulators are treating crypto deposit-taking as unlicensed securities activity with personal liability, raising the cost of capital for any yield-bearing consumer protocol.

top_signals.title: Sen. Blumenthal seeks answers from Tether over payments to firm founded by ex-White House crypto adviser
top_signals.summary: Senator Blumenthal has sent a letter to Tether requesting records regarding its business dealings with Nxum and Bo Hines. The inquiry focuses on payments made to a firm founded by a former White House crypto adviser.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Blumenthal's Tether inquiry shows stablecoin issuers now face congressional oversight of their political relationships, adding a new dimension of Washington risk to the premium investors underwrite on reserve transparency.

top_signals.title: Issuers Object to OKX-ICE’s Stock Tokenization Plans
top_signals.summary: Stock issuers are opposing the plans by OKX and ICE to tokenize equities. This conflict highlights the tension between traditional financial issuers and the push for blockchain-based asset representation.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Issuer opposition to OKX-ICE tokenization reveals that the value in equity tokenization accrues to whoever controls the primary listing relationship, not the blockchain rail, which undermines the 'disintermediation' thesis for this vertical.

on_the_radar.title: Bitcoin Core changes security policy as AI makes bugs easier to find
on_the_radar.summary: Bitcoin Core is updating its security disclosure policy to accelerate the release of vulnerability fixes. This change is a response to the increasing ability of AI tools to discover software bugs.

on_the_radar.title: IRS plans lower tax disclosure penalties, including for crypto: Forbes35m, IRS plans lower tax disclosure penalties, including for crypto: ForbesThe US tax agency is targeting faster resolutions and more flexible payment options for taxpayers voluntarily disclosing past tax violations under a planned program overhaul.
on_the_radar.summary: The IRS is planning to overhaul its voluntary disclosure program to offer lower penalties and more flexible payment options for taxpayers. This initiative specifically includes those disclosing past tax violations related to cryptocurrency holdings.

on_the_radar.title: Initia halts blockchain after exploit reportedly drains over $2.6M12m
on_the_radar.summary: Initia has halted its blockchain operations following a security exploit. The attack reportedly resulted in the loss of over $2.6 million.

on_the_radar.title: Solana Alpenglow Upgrade Ships. Adoption is the Real Test
on_the_radar.summary: The Solana network has implemented the Alpenglow upgrade, aimed at improving network stability and performance. The focus now shifts toward whether these technical improvements will drive increased real-world adoption.

on_the_radar.title: Raffles Family Office is building a wealth manager for Asia’s stablecoin billionaires
on_the_radar.summary: Raffles Family Office is developing a specialized wealth management service tailored for high-net-worth individuals in Asia holding significant stablecoin assets. The initiative aims to bridge the gap between digital asset wealth and traditional banking infrastructure.

on_the_radar.title: Was crypto self-custody ever designed for beginners?
on_the_radar.summary: Crypto executives are debating the accessibility and safety of self-custody for beginners following security incidents involving Ledger and Coldcard. The discussion focuses on whether simplifying hardware wallet design can reduce user error and improve security for private investors.

on_the_radar.title: Cysic dangles a 10% bounty, hacker pours loot into Tornado Cash
on_the_radar.summary: A hacker who attacked the Cysic bridge has moved approximately $744,000 in ETH and BNB to Tornado Cash. This action follows an offer from the Cysic foundation of a 10% bounty for the recovery of the stolen funds.

on_the_radar.title: Bitcoin slides below $81,500 as tech stock sell-off spreads to Asian equities
on_the_radar.summary: Bitcoin's price has dropped below $81,500 following a broader market sell-off. The decline is linked to a tech stock slump in Wall Street and Asian equities driven by AI spending concerns and geopolitical tensions.

linkedin_post:
Three ASEAN central banks just agreed to share a stablecoin rail. HSBC put a Hong Kong dollar stablecoin in two million retail wallets. Same week. Same asset class. Two completely different bets on where the value collects.

The BLOOM expansion is governments underwriting infrastructure. HSBC's RedCoin is a bank capturing the user relationship. Both use stablecoins. Neither needs crypto-native issuers. That's the repricing.

We've been underwriting stablecoin plays on reserve yield and network effects. The Asian moves this week suggest the real moat may be regulatory pre-approval and existing KYC pools. HSBC didn't build a new wallet. It used PayMe. The central banks didn't invent a standard. They adopted Ripple, Visa, Mastercard.

Meanwhile Senator Blumenthal is asking Tether about payments to a firm tied to a former White House adviser. The scrutiny is getting specific. Political relationship risk is now a line item.

The test: in twelve months, does RedCoin transaction volume show retail users preferring bank-issued stablecoins for payments? If yes, the issuer premium shifts hard to tradfi balance sheets and licensed e-money frameworks. If no, then the compliance cost was deadweight and crypto-native speed still wins.

We're watching the PayMe data. Not the white papers.
